page: Microsoft Azure E128-64s_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is equipped with 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. It achieves top-tier results in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds of 391.59 GB/sec and write speeds of 171.9 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is rated strong, supported by a Passmark CPU score of 76622.09 and a top-tier physics test score. Database operations are highly efficient, registering 35230.63 on Passmark database benchmarks and 85.44 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

The server's hardware profile offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads due to its massive 1 TB memory capacity paired with dedicated compute resources. However, certain tradeoffs exist: the instance includes no local storage, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage, and contains zero GPUs, which limits its applicability for heavy graphics or large-scale parallel deep learning training. Additionally, it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Microsoft Azure E128-64s_v6 is suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Its high memory capacity and strong database benchmark performance make it an appropriate fit for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data-dense enterprise applications. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions also enables efficient CPU-based machine learning inference, as demonstrated by strong prompt processing speeds on small and medium LLM models.
